issues.finding: The property that N is transitive is relativized to N rather than to the ambient model M. The internal existential statement supplies the property as evaluated in M; restricting it to N cannot justify the following external claim.
issues.proposed_resolution: Relativize the transitivity-and-potency condition on N to M, then use the closure of transitive potent M to pass it to the ambient universe.

issues.location: Potter proof and first exercise, Separation schema for inner sets
issues.finding: Transitivity alone does not make an arbitrary set satisfy relativized Separation; the separated subset of a member need not belong to the set. This also undermines the Montague proof's reused minimal-model predicate for the Potter extension.
issues.proposed_resolution: Require the inner model to be transitive and potent (closed under subsets of its members), strengthen the minimal-model predicate and its witness displays accordingly, and state the repaired Separation exercise with that antecedent.

translation_treatment: The target strengthens the minimal transitive theta-model to a transitive potent one, fixes the ambient relativization superscript, and makes the Potter argument and exercise require potency for Separation. Frozen English source bytes are unchanged.
